newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says Jakarta not claiming Busang rights.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says Jakarta not claiming Busang rights.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Tuesday that the letter it received from the Indonesian government did not claim the right to manage the huge Busang gold deposit.
"It does not contain in there that 'the government will have full right to manage Busang II and III.' It's not in there," Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said in a phone interview from Calgary.
Reuters in Jakarta obtained a copy of the letter on Monday and reported that it gave Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp one month to settle with their local partners in Busang.

"If in that one month that agreement mentioned is not achieved, then everything that had been discussed previously will be cancelled, and the government will have full right to further manage Busang II and III," the Reuters copy of the letter said.
But McAnulty said Bre-X had its letter translated by several different sources and that none of the translations included any mention of the government having full rights to manage Busang II and III.
"Not one of them has anything after the word 'cancelled'," McAnulty said.
He said Bre-X would release a statement likely later today explaining its response to the letter from Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana.
"The investing public should be very careful in its interpretation of recent articles pertaining to this letter," McAnulty said.
Barrick officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
Bre-X and gold firm Barrick agreed last month to split the Busang deposit, with Bre-X keeping 22.5 percent, Barrick getting 67.5 percent and the rest going to the Indonesian government.
The companies presented their proposal to the government with a request for clarification to a few issues.
The letter from Sudjana was the government's response to the Bre-X and Barrick proposal.
The Busang deposit is estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
